# Create combat gym scene for combat-coupled power-ups (P3 Shield, P4 Bomb, P6 Phase Shift, P7 Teleport) with low-level enemy threats

## Problem statement

Four power-up types in the GDD catalogue — **P3 Shield, P4 Bomb, P6 Phase Shift, P7 Teleport** — cannot demonstrate their full behaviour without threats: Shield must absorb a hit, Bomb must clear on-screen enemy bullets, Phase Shift must pass through enemies and bullets, and Teleport must search for a safe spot free of threats. The operator split these "combat-coupled" types out of the threat-free power-up gym (AH-0MTC0QPS60005MNT) into this dedicated **combat gym scene** that contains a **low-level enemy threat (E1 Scout with shooting)**. The scene shares the round-robin spawn lifecycle, grow-shrink animation, 3% collection threshold, player ship, and standalone HUD class with the non-combat gym, on which this item depends.

## Users

- **Player / developer testing the game** — wants to see each combat-coupled power-up's full effect against real (but low-level) threats: a shield bubble popping on a hit, a bomb wiping a bullet cloud, ghosting straight through a formation, and blinking away to a safe spot.
- **AI agents / developers implementing AI_Hell** — need the threat-coupled behaviour (hit absorption, bullet clearing, intangibility, safe-spot resolution) implemented and tested once, in a form the main game can reuse.

### Example user stories

- As a **player**, I want my shield bubble to absorb exactly one hit and pop, so I can verify the GDD's "absorbs one hit" rule.
- As a **player**, I want to collect a Bomb while scouts are firing and see every on-screen enemy bullet vanish, with enemies untouched (they are 1 HP, GDD §4.4).
- As a **player**, I want Phase Shift to let me fly straight through the scout formation and its bullets without being hit, for 3 seconds.
- As a **player**, I want to press Space with a collected Teleport to jump to the nearest safe spot (free of scouts and bullets) along my travel direction, gaining Phase Shift on arrival.
- As a **developer**, I want the ship's hit response (no shield/phase shift) to be a simple flash/reset with no lives counter, so the demo keeps a pure combat focus.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Combat scene with ship + low-level threats:** A new `GymPowerUpsCombat` scene (key `GymPowerUpsCombat`, label `PowerUps Combat`) is defined in `src/scenes/gym/`, auto-discovered and listed by the gym index, boots correctly, renders the player ship with standard thrust movement + screen-wrap, and contains a **formation of E1 Scout enemies** (reusing `src/entities/Scout.ts` + the formation utilities) with a **SHOOT toggle** that enables aimed enemy fire at the **ship's live position** (not the fixed demo target), so hits are demonstrable. Shared "← INDEX" back button present.
- [ ] **AC2 — Round-robin spawn/lifecycle:** The scene spawns exactly the combat-coupled power-ups **P3, P4, P6, P7 in ascending GDD order**, one every 5 s, each remaining stationary for a 5 s lifetime; spawn = **grow from scale 0 to full size**, despawn = **shrink to nothing**; growth/shrink delta-time driven with the same tunable constants as the non-combat gym (AH-0MTC0QPS60005MNT).
- [ ] **AC3 — Collection rule:** A drop is collectible only while its current scale is **> 3% of full size** (grow, hold, and shrink until below threshold); collection requires the ship to overlap the drop; an uncollected drop fades with no effect.
- [ ] **AC4 — P3 Shield full behaviour:** Collecting P3 arms a shield bubble rendered around the ship for **15 s**; the bubble **absorbs exactly one hit** (enemy body or enemy bullet) and then pops (effect ends, no ship flash/reset for that hit); if never hit, it expires after 15 s. Re-collection while active refreshes the timer to 15 s.
- [ ] **AC5 — P4 Bomb full behaviour:** Collecting P4 instantly removes **all on-screen enemy bullets** (aimed scout fire in-flight), does **not damage enemies** (GDD §4.4 note), is not a timed effect, and shows a brief HUD notice. Re-collection while enemies are not firing is a benign no-op (bullets cleared anyway).
- [ ] **AC6 — P6 Phase Shift full behaviour:** Collecting P6 renders a ghost-outline ship for **3 s** during which the ship **passes through enemy bodies and enemy bullets without being hit**; hit checks are disabled for the duration. Re-collection refreshes the timer to 3 s.
- [ ] **AC7 — P7 Teleport full behaviour:** P7 **stacks FIFO** (each pickup = one use); pressing **Space** consumes the earliest-collected use and teleports the ship **along the current travel direction to the nearest safe spot** — a position free of enemy bodies and enemy bullets in a safety radius, clamped to screen bounds; if no safe spot exists in the travel direction, the ship teleports to the nearest on-screen safe position anyway; on arrival the ship **gains P6 Phase Shift (3 s)** per GDD. HUD shows the teleport count.
- [ ] **AC8 — Hit response (no shield/phase shift):** Being hit by an enemy body or enemy bullet with no active P3/P6 triggers a **simple flash/reset with no lives counter** (e.g., brief invulnerability + reposition), per operator decision; this is the only consequence — no lives, no game over.
- [ ] **AC9 — HUD reuse:** The scene uses the **standalone HUD class from AH-0MTC0QPS60005MNT** (`src/ui/HUD.ts`) unchanged for active-effect icons, names, timers (P3/P6), and counts (P7); **no lives counter** in this scene; the HUD class itself is not modified with gym/combat-specific logic (any extension lives in the scene).
- [ ] **AC10 — Testing/validation:** Unit tests cover: P3 absorb-then-pop on a hit + 15 s expiry + refresh; P4 clearing all bullets without enemy damage; P6 pass-through (no hits during 3 s) + refresh; P7 FIFO stack/consume, safe-spot resolution (avoiding scouts/bullets, clamped), fallback when no safe spot, and P6-on-arrival; hit-response flash/reset (no lives); round-robin order. Scene-level tests (gameHarness) verify discovery, ship presence, scout formation + SHOOT toggle, collection against live bullets, and back button. Full suite green.
- [ ] **AC11 — Documentation:** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries (GDD §6.4 architecture gains `GymPowerUpsCombat`).
- [ ] **AC12 — Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Engine/stack:** Phaser v4 + TypeScript, Vite, Vitest (locked). Neon-vector aesthetic; code-drawn graphics only — **no external art assets**; icons code-drawn per GDD §4.4 suggestions.
- **Threats:** **E1 Scout only** (operator decision) — reuse `src/entities/Scout.ts` as-is; formation via existing utilities; **shooting toggle** enabled for the demo (bullets aimed at the ship's live position). No E2/E3/E4/E5/Boss.
- **No lives model:** hit response is flash/reset only (operator decision); P8 lives is out of scope (it lives in the non-combat gym).
- **Weapon power-ups out of scope:** P1/P2/new weapon patterns belong to AH-0MTC1TEXR006I5XR; the ship's auto-fire is NOT part of this scene (Bomb does not damage enemies, so no fire needed).
- **Shared mechanics:** the spawn cadence (one per 5 s, 5 s lifetime, 0.5 s grow/shrink) and the 3% collection threshold match the non-combat gym (AH-0MTC0QPS60005MNT); constants stay in `src/core/constants.ts`; the HUD class is reused unchanged (dependency on that item).
- **Hit model details:** overlap = ship hull radius + enemy/bullet radius, exactly as the GDD "enemies are the bullets" §2.4 model; shield/phase-shift suppress the hit response; teleport safe radius is a tunable constant (proposal: ~3× ship size).

## Existing state

- Non-combat power-up gym **AH-0MTC0QPS60005MNT** (intake_complete, open) delivers, first: `src/powerups/PowerUp.ts` (base lifecycle), the type catalogue + icons, `src/ui/HUD.ts` (standalone), the spawn/lifecycle constants, and `GymPowerUps` — **this item depends on those reusable pieces**. This item adds the P3/P4/P6/P7 catalogue entries + threat-coupled effect hooks.
- `src/entities/Scout.ts` exists with `tryFireAimedBullet` (currently aimed at a fixed demo target), formation offsets, alive/destroy lifecycle; `GymScout` demonstrates a V-formation with EXPLODE/SHOOT buttons via the shared `GymFormationScene` core library (`src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts`).
- Ship + thrust movement exist (`src/entities/Player.ts`, `src/utils/movement.ts`, `GymPlayer.ts`).
- GDD §4.4 defines P3/P4/P6/P7 semantics and icon suggestions; §4.4 notes Bomb does not damage 1-HP enemies; §2.3 lives model (out of scope here, replaced by flash/reset).
- Tests use Vitest + a gameHarness (`src/test/gameHarness.ts`) with happy-dom.

## Desired change

1. Extend the power-up catalogue from AH-0MTC0QPS60005MNT with **P3/P4/P6/P7** entries (id, name, icon, duration/stack semantics, threat-coupled effect hooks), following the same `src/powerups/` layout.
2. Add `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsCombat.ts` — ship (reused `Player` + movement), a Scout V-formation with a SHOOT toggle (bullets aimed at the ship), the shared round-robin spawner (P3 → P4 → P6 → P7), grow/hold/shrink lifecycle, 3% collection gate, threat-coupled effect application (shield absorb, bomb clear, phase shift pass-through, teleport safe-spot), flash/reset hit response, HUD attachment (reused), back button.
3. Ship-aimed fire: extend or parameterise the Scout's fire target so bullets aim at the ship's live position (implementation may pass the ship position into the scene's fire-collection path).
4. Add safe-spot resolution (enemy/bullet-aware) + teleport consumption to `src/powerups/effects.ts`; add hit-check suppression for shield/phase-shift in the scene collision pass.
5. Update the GDD §6.4 architecture briefly (list `GymPowerUpsCombat`; note threat-coupled effects as implemented).
6. Tests: unit tests for P3/P4/P6/P7 behaviours + scene tests via gameHarness.

## Key Files:

- `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsCombat.ts` — **new** combat gym scene (the deliverable).
- `src/powerups/types.ts` — extend the catalogue from AH-0MTC0QPS60005MNT with **P3/P4/P6/P7** entries.
- `src/powerups/effects.ts` — extend with shield-absorb state, bomb bullet-clear, phase-shift hit suppression, teleport safe-spot resolution + FIFO consumption.
- `src/powerups/icons.ts` — extend with P3/P4/P6/P7 code-drawn icons.
- `src/powerups/PowerUp.ts` — **reused** (depends on AH-0MTC0QPS60005MNT).
- `src/ui/HUD.ts` — **reused unchanged** (depends on AH-0MTC0QPS60005MNT).
- `src/entities/Scout.ts` — possibly parameterised aim target (ship position) for `tryFireAimedBullet`.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsCombat.test.ts` (+ P3/P4/P6/P7 unit tests) — **new** tests.
- `src/core/constants.ts` — teleport safe radius + travelled distance, hit-reset values (extend the shared constants).
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — §6.4 architecture: add `GymPowerUpsCombat`.

## Related work

- **AH-0MTC0QPS60005MNT** — "Create gym scene for power-ups with spawning, collection, and standalone HUD" (the non-combat gym): **prerequisite** — supplies the shared PowerUp lifecycle, catalogue, icons, HUD class, and spawn/lifecycle constants this item reuses/extends. Dependency edge: this item → AH-0MTC0QPS60005MNT.
- **AH-0MTC1TEXR006I5XR** — "Weapon power-ups (3 patterns + reset) with auto-fire and weapon gym scene" (in-progress): sibling — weapon power-ups excluded here, same round-robin/grow-shrink/3% mechanics.
- **"Create E1 Scout gym scene" / GymScout** — precedent for the Scout formation, EXPLODE/SHOOT buttons, and the `GymFormationScene` core-library pattern (AH-0MT994ESD000RP1Q completed; core-library refactor AH-0MT987VA3005YBNK / AH-0MTAN4IFR007U9B3 completed).
- **"Create gym scene with player ship and thrust-based space movement" (AH-0MT97OA3E001DOYW)** — precedent for `Player` reuse.
- GDD power-up catalog items (completed): "Redesign P7 Dash…" (AH-0MT7UY5UR002LD5U), "Add a Magnet power up" (AH-0MT7VE4SX0005A8V), "Add an extra life power up" (AH-0MT7UX8LE0072MR3) — semantics source for P7/P9/P8 (P3/P4/P6 remain as defined in GDD §4.4).
- GDD items (completed): "Game Design Document for AI_Hell" (AH-0MT7O8KCY0059RA5).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Dependency:** this item assumes the non-combat gym (AH-0MTC0QPS60005MNT) lands first (PowerUp lifecycle, catalogue, HUD, constants). If that item is delayed, the combat scene work is blocked — do not build parallel copies of the lifecycle/HUD.
- **Assumption — ship-aimed fire:** Scout's `tryFireAimedBullet` currently aims at a fixed demo target; the combat scene requires bullets aimed at the ship's live position. Implement by parameterising the aim target (small, contained change) rather than duplicating the Scout entity.
- **Assumption — teleport safe spot:** "nearest safe spot in the travel direction" = first empty position along the travel ray where no enemy body or bullet occupies a safety-radius disc (tunable, proposal 3× ship size), clamped to screen bounds; fallback = nearest on-screen safe position (GDD); P6 granted on arrival.
- **Assumption — hit response flash/reset:** a hit without shield/phase shift flashes the ship and repositions it (or grants brief invulnerability) — exact demo values tunable; no lives, no game over (operator Q8).
- **Assumption — scout formation counts as the "low-level threat":** default V-formation of ~6 scouts with drift (as GymScout), SHOOT toggle default OFF so the operator/player can turn fire on for the demo.
- **Scope-creep guard:** E2/E3/E4/E5/Boss threats, weapon autofire, lives/score, leaderboard, and the non-combat power-ups (P5/P8/P9) are out of scope; record any extras as linked work items.
- **Risk — sibling drift:** same constants/mechanics as the two sibling gyms; coordinate to keep the shared lifecycle consistent (extract a shared util if a third consumer appears).

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- Q1 (this round): "Which enemies constitute 'low level enemy threats' — reuse existing E1 Scout/E2 Diver/E3 Tank entities with bullet-firing, or generic placeholders?" — Answer (operator): **"1. Just use scout (with shooting)"** — the combat scene reuses the existing E1 Scout entity with its shooting enabled. Source: interactive reply.
- Q2 (this round): "Ship hit response in the combat gym — (a) lives with respawn (3 lives), (b) simple flash/reset without a lives counter, (c) other?" — Answer (operator): **"2. b"** — simple flash/reset, no lives counter (pure demo). Source: interactive reply.
- Q3 (scope split, previous round): "Separate the combat-coupled power-ups (P3/P4/P6/P7) into their own work item and combat scene with low-level enemy threats?" — Answer (operator): **"Separate out the combat coupled items into a different work item and different combat scene. That scene should contain low level enemy threats."** — implemented as this item; the threat-free gym (AH-0MTC0QPS60005MNT) keeps P5/P8/P9 and the shared lifecycle/HUD. Source: interactive reply.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MT994ESD000RP1Q** – Create E1 Scout gym scene (completed)
- **AH-0MTAJO038004ILN8** – Gym index browser crash from bundled test files (completed)
- **AH-0MT7O8KCY0059RA5** – Game Design Document for AI_Hell (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: 0mt7o8kcy0059ra5, 0mt7ve4sx0005a8v, absorb, absorbs, ac1 (+302 more)
- `README.md` — matched: ac3, ac4, ac5, acceptance, active (+276 more)
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: active, add, agents, aim, aimed (+178 more)

# Tank has no audio (AH-0MTCNZAPS007WTQE)

**Headline:** The E3 Tank fires 10-projectile radial bursts completely silently and has no Tank-identity audio on destruction. Add a Tank-specific mechanical-whine advance cue flowing with NO gap into a heavy cannon-thump fire sound (one cue+thump pair per burst, scene-level, at the moment of firing), following the established procedural-audio pattern; destruction reuses the shared `playDestructionSound()` already played by the base scene (no double-play). Update GDD §7.3 to record that audio-character decisions are made per-enemy at implementation, with a cross-reference to the enemy design doc, and add this item's best practices to `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`.

## Problem statement

Tanks (`src/entities/Tank.ts`, gym scene `src/scenes/gym/GymTank.ts`) fire radial bursts silently — `tryFireRadialBurst()` spawns 10 projectiles with no audio — and they are indistinguishable aurally from any other enemy on destruction (only the generic shared destruction sound plays; the Tank-specific `playTankDestructionSound()` in `src/audio/effects.ts` is defined but never wired up). The Tank breaks the GDD §7.3 audio-feedback design (enemy fire should be announced) and is inconsistent with its peers (Scout has a fire sound + advance cue; Swarm has a volley burst sound; Phaser has an advance cue + destruction sound).

## Users

- **Players** — need audible feedback when a Tank fires its radial burst (a heavy, mechanical "cannon" cue) and an advance warning so the burst is telegraphed, per GDD §7.3.
- **AI agents / developers implementing AI_Hell** — need Tank audio to follow the established procedural-audio pattern (`src/audio/effects.ts`) so headless tests stay green and the enemy core-library best practices apply.

### Example user stories

- As a player, I want to hear a heavy cannon thump when a tank fires its radial burst so I can react to the projectiles.
- As a player, I want a mechanical-whine advance cue before a tank fires so I can anticipate the burst, without an awkward dead gap between warning and shot.
- As a developer, I want Tank audio implemented via the existing `effects.ts` helpers so it degrades to a safe no-op in headless tests and never double-plays the destruction sound.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Fire sound + advance cue** — A new Tank fire sound plays exactly **once per radial burst** (not per projectile): a heavy low "cannon thump" (`playTankFireSound()`, new). Preceded by a mechanical-whine advance cue (`playTankAdvanceCue()`, new) that flows into the thump with **no gap** (whine duration still provides the ≥ 500 ms advance lead per GDD §7.3).
- **Scene-level orchestration, one cue per burst** — `GymTank` orchestrates the cue+thump pair at the point of shooting, once per burst (Swarm-style scene-level pattern: when new bullets appear in the update loop, play the pair exactly once), not per entity/projectile.
- **Destruction sound (reuse)** — Destroying a Tank plays the shared `playDestructionSound()` exactly once per destruction (already satisfied by `GymFormationScene`). The Tank must NOT add its own destruction-sound call (no double-play); the unused `playTankDestructionSound()` is left un-wired (dead code) or removed by the implementer — not used for fire.
- **Safe degradation** — All new audio calls are safe no-ops without a working `AudioContext` (headless tests, browsers without Web Audio), preserving the `effects.ts` contract.
- **Documentation** — GDD §7.3 updated to record that audio-character decisions are made per-enemy at implementation and to cross-reference `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`; the enemy design doc's §3.2 GymTank row changed from "none" to the new audio pattern and §7 best-practices updated with this item's guidance (no-gap cue→thump for Tank, per-enemy audio character). All related documentation (code comments, README as applicable) updated. CHANGELOG.md excluded (ship skill owns it).
- **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Procedural Web Audio only — no audio assets (existing `effects.ts` pattern).
- Follow enemy core-library best practices (`docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`); the base `GymFormationScene` already plays spawn/destruction sounds for all enemy gyms — reconcile entity-level vs scene-level audio to avoid double-play.
- Audio functions must degrade to safe no-ops in headless environments.
- Do not include CI/CD pipeline tests.

## Existing state

- `src/entities/Tank.ts` — `tryFireRadialBurst()` spawns `TANK_BURST_COUNT = 10` projectiles silently; no audio imports. Fire interval `TANK_FIRE_INTERVAL = 2400` ms; bursts are per-entity but the scene collects them.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymTank.ts` — thin `GymFormationScene` subclass; `collectBullets` returns `tank.tryFireRadialBurst(now)`; no audio calls.
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` — base class plays `playSpawnSound()` at spawn and `playDestructionSound()` in `explodeRandom()` and `_handleCollisions()` for all enemy gyms (design doc §6/§7: base-class-owned).
- `src/audio/effects.ts` — `playTankDestructionSound()` (220→30 Hz sawtooth, 0.45 s, vol 0.2 — "heavier, lower destruction cue") is currently **dead code** (defined, never called). Has `playSpawnSound`, `playDestructionSound`, power-up/weapon cues, `playSwarmBurstSound`, `playScoutFireSound`, `playScoutAdvanceCue`; **no Tank fire sound or advance cue exists**.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymSwarm.ts` (reference pattern) — overrides `update()` to count bullets before/after and calls `playSwarmBurstSound()` exactly once when new bullets appear (coordinated volley).
- `src/entities/Scout.ts` (reference) — two-phase tell: advance cue at tell start, then a gap, then fire sound + shot. Operator explicitly wants the Tank to have NO gap (and flagged Scout for the same treatment — see related work).
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` §3.2 — table lists `GymTank` audio as "none"; §7 no-double-play rule.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` §7.3 — SFX catalog: "Enemy fire (Level 4+)" = Short zap, Low-medium, Immediate; advance telegraphing requires ≥ 500 ms lead for Level 4–5 enemy fire. No per-enemy audio-character notes; no cross-reference to the enemy design doc.
- `README.md` — does not document per-enemy Tank audio (only Scout/Boss cues); leave untouched unless discovered otherwise.

## Desired change

- **New sounds** in `src/audio/effects.ts`: `playTankAdvanceCue()` (mechanical whine, ≥ 500 ms, leading straight into the shot with no gap) and `playTankFireSound()` (heavy low cannon thump), both safe no-ops without an `AudioContext`.
- **Scene orchestration** in `GymTank` (model: `GymSwarm.update()`): when the update loop detects new bullets (a burst fired), play the advance cue immediately followed by the fire thump with no gap — exactly one cue+thump pair per burst.
- **Destruction**: no entity change — reuse the shared `playDestructionSound()` already played by the base scene; test asserts no double-play. The existing unused `playTankDestructionSound()` is NOT used for firing; implementer wires it or removes it as dead code (see Q2 appendix).
- **Docs**: GDD §7.3 note + cross-reference; enemy design doc §3.2 row + §7 best practices from this item.

**Key Files:**

- `src/audio/effects.ts` — add `playTankAdvanceCue()` and `playTankFireSound()` (procedural Web Audio, safe no-op guard); decide fate of dead `playTankDestructionSound()`.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymTank.ts` — override `update()` (Swarm pattern) to detect new bullets and play the cue+thump pair once per burst at the point of shooting.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymTank.test.ts` — add spy-based tests: one cue+thump pair per burst, cue precedes thump with no gap, no double destruction sound, headless no-op degradation (see `GymSwarm.test.ts` / `GymScout.test.ts` for the established test pattern).
- `src/entities/Tank.test.ts` — only if firing-path changes require entity-level assertions; prefer scene-level tests.
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` — no change expected (base class already owns spawn/destruction audio).
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — §7.3: per-enemy audio-character decision note + cross-reference to `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`.
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — §3.2 `GymTank` audio column from "none" to the new pattern; §7 best-practices additions (no-gap cue→thump for Tank, per-enemy audio character allowed).
- `README.md` — only if it documents per-enemy Tank audio (checked: it does not; leave untouched unless discovered otherwise).

## Related work

- **Swarm has no audio (AH-0MTCO1L74003CAQJ)** — in_review; the sibling item that added Swarm audio (scene-level volley burst sound, no advance cue) — the orchestration pattern for this item.
- **Scout has no audio (AH-0MTCO1LDA008RA19)** — completed; sibling that added Scout fire sound + advance cue (per-entity two-phase tell with a gap — the gap this item's operator feedback flags for removal).
- **Remove the gap between Scout advance cue and shot (AH-0MTF1I1S8003P0GU)** — created from this intake (discovered-from), operator-requested follow-up: apply the same no-gap treatment to Scout.
- **Ensure enemy best practices document include instructions for audio on spawn, shoot and explode (AH-0MTCNZFCD009P5IB)** — open, sibling; overlaps with this item's documentation ACs.
- **Create E3 Tank gym scene (AH-0MT99I2OC0014MNZ)** — completed; created the scene/entity this item extends.
- **Update E4/E5/Boss work items to adhere to core-library best practices (AH-0MTAN51HO007A92H)** — completed; established the `effects.ts` audio pattern and base-class audio ownership.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Double-play risk**: the base `GymFormationScene` plays `playDestructionSound()` in both destruction paths. The Tank must NOT call it in its own explosion path (design doc §7). Assumption: "reuse" (Q3) confirms the shared destruction sound; the once-only guarantee is an AC.
- **No-gap cue timing**: the mechanical whine must still satisfy the GDD ≥ 500 ms advance-lead requirement while flowing into the thump with no dead gap. Assumption: whine duration itself provides the lead (cue starts ≥ 500 ms before the shot lands); implementer to verify exact timing in tests (cue → thump ordering, minimal gap).
- **Scene-level orchestration**: bursts are collected scene-level (`collectBullets`); the Swarm-style new-bullet detection in `GymTank.update()` is the established pattern. Assumption: one cue+thump pair per burst is acceptable even if two tanks fire in nearly the same frame (operator: "one", not per-entity).
- **Dead-code `playTankDestructionSound()`**: defined but unused; the implementer either leaves it untouched or removes it — it must NOT be repurposed as the fire sound (operator: "new", Q2 round 2).
- **Testability**: existing enemy tests do not exercise audio; new tests spy/mock `src/audio/effects` to assert call counts/ordering in headless runs.
- **Scope creep**: no other enemy audio work is implied (Diver is a separate pre-existing open item AH-0MTCO1LGD0082SVG; the Scout gap is tracked in AH-0MTF1I1S8003P0GU). Record extra opportunities as linked work items, not scope.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 (round 1)**: Fire sound character — single heavy low "cannon thump" per burst (one sound for the 10-shot radial burst, scene-level, Swarm-style) or a short zap per GDD §7.3 catalog wording? — **Answer (producer): "1. heavy thump (update the GDD to allow this kind of decision without questioning the producer)"** — heavy cannon thump; GDD must record that audio-character decisions are per-enemy at implementation. Source: interactive reply.
- **Q2 (round 1)**: Advance warning cue — ≥ 500 ms warning before each burst (Scout/Phaser pattern) or no cue (Swarm post-playtest)? — **Answer (producer): "2. advance warning"** — the Tank gets an advance warning cue. Source: interactive reply.
- **Q3 (round 1)**: Destruction sound — reuse shared `playDestructionSound()` or wire the existing unused `playTankDestructionSound()` heavier boom? — **Answer (producer): "3. reuse"** — reuse the shared destruction sound; no double-play. Source: interactive reply.
- **Q1 (round 2)**: Advance cue sound character? — **Answer (producer): "1. mechanical whine with no gap between this and the thump of the shot"** — mechanical whine advance cue flowing directly into the cannon thump with no dead gap. Source: interactive reply.

The Swarm enemy (E5) currently has no audio feedback at all. Per GDD §7.3, the Swarm needs coordinated fire sounds (volley burst) and explosion/destruction sounds to give the player clear auditory cues about enemy behaviour.

## Requirements

1. **Destruction sound**: Reuse the existing `playDestructionSound()` function (already plays in `GymFormationScene.explodeRandom()` for all enemies). Swarm should NOT call it in its own `playExplosion()` to avoid double-play. The base scene owns destruction sound.

2. **Swarm burst fire sound**: Create a new `playSwarmBurstSound()` in `src/audio/effects.ts` that plays a single coordinated volley-level sound (buzzing/whoosh) — the entire swarm fires simultaneously, so one sound should represent the whole burst.

3. **Single sound per volley**: Only one burst sound per coordinated volley, not one per entity. The scene (`GymSwarm`) orchestrates this: when new bullets appear in the update loop, play the volley sound exactly once.

4. **Advance audio cue** (removed per operator feedback): Originally requested a ≥ 500 ms warning cue before firing (mirroring Phaser). This was removed in post-playtest feedback — the operator noted the advance cue was "disconnected, not a warning of a shot coming." The fire sound now plays at the exact point of shooting.

5. **Headless test safety**: All new audio functions must degrade to safe no-ops in headless/test environments (return early if `getAudioContext()` is null).

## Implementation Plan

- `src/audio/effects.ts`: Add `playSwarmBurstSound()` (sawtooth + sine oscillators, ~200ms duration)
- `src/entities/Swarm.ts`: Fire sound at point of shooting (single-phase: no advance cue)
- `src/scenes/gym/GymSwarm.ts`: Override `update()` to detect new bullets and play `playSwarmBurstSound()` once per volley
- `src/scenes/gym/GymFormationScene.ts`: No changes needed (base class already handles destruction sound)
- Tests: Update existing Swarm tests for single-phase firing; add volley-level burst sound test with `vi.spyOn`; add headless no-op tests
- Documentation: Update `ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` with audio orchestration details

## Operator Feedback (post-playtest)

- The firing audio was disconnected (advance cue warning) — removed advance cue. Fire sound now plays at the exact point of shooting (scene-level volley sound in GymSwarm.update). 
- Explosion was too quiet — increased playDestructionSound() volume from 0.15 to 0.3.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Destruction sound plays exactly once per destruction — GymFormationScene.explodeRandom() calls playDestructionSound() once; Swarm entity does not self-play, avoiding double-play (volume bumped from 0.15 to 0.3 for audibility).
2. New Swarm burst fire sound exists in src/audio/effects.ts — playSwarmBurstSound() exported.
3. Single volley-level sound per burst — GymSwarm.update() plays once per frame with new bullets; test verifies callCount < formationSwarms.length.
4. No advance cue — fire sound plays at the exact point of shooting; advance-cue state machine removed from Swarm.ts and playSwarmAdvanceCue() removed from effects.ts.
5. All new audio calls degrade to safe no-ops in headless/test environments — effects.ts getAudioContext() guard on all functions.
6. Documentation updated — ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md updated with audio orchestration details.
7. Full project test suite passes — npx vitest run (397 tests, 27 files) at commit a9d8a4e.
8. Explosion audibility — playDestructionSound() volume increased from 0.15 to 0.3.

# Add player to each Enemy Gym scene (AH-0MTD0Z0Y7003T1NT)

## Problem statement

The five enemy gym scenes — E1 Scout (`GymScout`), E2 Diver (`GymDiver`), E3 Tank
(`GymTank`), E4 Phaser (`GymPhaser`), E5 Swarm (`GymSwarm`) — contain **no player
ship**: enemies aim, fire, and dive at a fixed bottom-centre stand-in position
(documented as "standing in for the player"). Add the real, keyboard-controlled
`Player` ship to each scene with live combat interaction, so the enemy behaviour
is demonstrated against an actual target and the scenes double as combat
testbeds.

## Users

- **Developers / AI agents implementing AI_Hell** — want enemy-gym scenes that
  demonstrate enemy AI against the real player ship, with working combat
  feedback (hits, deaths, explosions), so behaviour can be verified in context.

### Example user stories

- As a **developer**, I want the Scout's aimed shots and the Diver's dive to
  track the *actual* player position, so I can verify L4+ behaviours against a
  moving target.
- As a **developer**, I want to fly the player ship (arrows + WASD) through each
  enemy gym, auto-firing, so I can test that player bullets destroy enemies
  (with explosion VFX/SFX) and enemy bullets hit the ship (explosion + respawn,
  infinite lives).
- As a **developer**, I want the closest-approach enemy bullets destroyed by
  player bullets, so fire-and-forget aiming feels responsive.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Player in every enemy gym scene:** `GymScout`, `GymDiver`,
  `GymTank`, `GymPhaser`, `GymSwarm` each spawn the existing `Player` ship
  (keyboard-controlled via arrows + WASD, using the shared input/movement
  plumbing), and the gym index still boots all five scenes.
- [ ] **AC2 — Live aim tracking:** enemy aimed fire (Scout shots, Diver dive,
  Swarm coordinated bursts, Phaser patterns per its telegraph rules) targets the
  player's current position each frame instead of the fixed bottom-centre
  stand-in. Tank radial burst (direction-agnostic) is unchanged.
- [ ] **AC3 — Combat interaction:** player auto-fires in the direction of travel
  (GDD §2.3, default Cannon, as in `GymWeapons`); player bullets destroy enemies
  (existing `destroySelf()` explosion VFX + SFX) and destroy enemy bullets.
- [ ] **AC4 — Player hit / respawn:** an enemy bullet hitting the player plays
  hit VFX + SFX and re-spawns the ship (explosion, brief re-spawn with
  invulnerability blink — infinite lives, no game-over state, no score change).
- [ ] **AC5 — Existing controls preserved:** the `EXPLODE` and `SHOOT: ON/OFF`
  HUD buttons remain; `SHOOT` keeps toggling enemy firing (L4+ simulation).
- [ ] **AC6 — Testing:** automated tests cover player spawn/control, live aim
  tracking, player-bullet ↔ enemy/bullet collisions, enemy-bullet → player hit +
  respawn (with invulnerability), and that existing scene behaviour is preserved;
  full project test suite passes.
- [ ] **AC7 — Docs:** `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` updated to
  document the player-in-enemy-gym convention (spawn, input, collisions,
  respawn); all related documentation updated to reflect the changes.

## Constraints

- Scenes are demonstration-only: **no game-over**, no lives counter, no scoring
  changes, no pause/level progression.
- Boss gym scene (**AH-0MT99QBDW001O7PE**) is **out of scope** — it does not
  exist yet and is tracked separately.
- Prefer extending the shared core library (`core/GymFormationScene.ts`) over
  per-scene boilerplate; keep the `EnemyFormationConfig` contract backward
  compatible (new fields optional/defaulted) so existing scenes and tests need
  minimal change. Follow `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` §5
  (smallest seam; core-library tests; contract compatibility).
- No collision engine — use manual distance checks in the scene update loop,
  consistent with existing gyms (`GymWeapons._overlapsShip`).
- Use the existing `Player` entity (`src/entities/Player.ts`) and
  `PlayerBullet` (`src/entities/PlayerBullet.ts`) — no net-new entity types.

## Existing state

- All five enemy gym scenes are thin `GymFormationScene<TEntity,TBullet>`
  subclasses (`src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts`): formation spawn,
  `EXPLODE`/`SHOOT` buttons, status/hint lines, `← INDEX` button, drift +
  respawn, bullet lifecycle. No player, no collisions, no input.
- Enemy entities (e.g. `Scout.target`, `Swarm.target`, `Diver.target`) hold a
  **fixed** aim target initialized to `(width/2, height-40)`; `Shoot` mode gates
  firing (`shootEnabled` toggled by the `SHOOT` button).
- `Player` is already wired with arrows+WASD input, thrust movement, and
  weapon/auto-fire in `GymPlayer`, `GymPowerUps`, `GymWeapons` (pattern:
  `new Player(...)` → `setInput` → `physicsTick`; auto-fire via `tryFire` +
  `createBulletsFromHeading`).
- Audio cues available: `playSpawnSound`, `playDestructionSound`,
  `playTankDestructionSound`, `playWeaponChangeSound` (`src/audio/effects.ts`).

## Desired change

- Add player spawn + input + auto-fire + collision handling to the **core
  formation scene** so all five scenes inherit it (per-scene opt-in/config if
  the seam needs it).
- Replace fixed enemy aim targets with per-frame updates to the player's live
  position.
- Player bullets destroy enemies (existing explosion path) and enemy bullets.
- Enemy bullets hitting the player trigger explode + respawn with
  invulnerability blink (infinite lives).
- Keep `EXPLODE` / `SHOOT` buttons; `SHOOT` continues to toggle enemy firing.

## Key Files

- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` — player spawn, keyboard input,
  auto-fire, collision checks (player↔enemy, player-bullet↔enemy-bullet,
  enemy-bullet↔player), respawn + invulnerability; backward-compatible
  `EnemyFormationConfig` extensions.
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.test.ts` — stub-driven tests for the
  new player/combat seams.
- `src/entities/Scout.ts`, `src/entities/Diver.ts`, `src/entities/Tank.ts`,
  `src/entities/Phaser.ts`, `src/entities/Swarm.ts` — live aim-target updates
  (replaces fixed bottom-centre target).
- `src/scenes/gym/GymScout.ts`, `GymDiver.ts`, `GymTank.ts`, `GymPhaser.ts`,
  `GymSwarm.ts` — thin wiring/accessors for player presence; possible entity
  aim-target plumbing.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymScout.test.ts`, `GymDiver.test.ts`, `GymTank.test.ts`,
  `GymPhaser.test.ts`, `GymSwarm.test.ts` — player/combat assertions +
  preserved-behaviour regression.
- `src/entities/Player.ts` / `src/entities/PlayerBullet.ts` — used as-is; small
  additions only if the respawn/invulnerability seam demands it.
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — player-in-enemy-gym best-practice
  section (spawn, input, collisions, respawn, testing).

## Related work

- Parent intent: `Create Enemy Gym Scene work items (AH-0MT987VA3005YBNK)`
  — original scope explicitly excluded player ships; this item revises that
  decision for E1–E5.
- `Refactor Enemy Gym Scenes (AH-0MT985FOA008JWM9)` — core library +
  `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`; this item extends that library.
- `Create Boss (Central AI) gym scene (AH-0MT99QBDW001O7PE)` — out of scope but
  should follow the convention established here when built.
- `Create combat gym scene for combat-coupled power-ups (AH-0MTC2P6G3007PJ40)`
  — overlapping combat-mechanics concerns (enemy bullets vs player), may reuse
  shared concepts.
- Reference player wiring: `GymWeapons.ts`, `GymPowerUps.ts`, `GymPlayer.ts`.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** adding player support to the shared core scene (with minimal
  per-scene config) is preferred over per-scene wiring — matches the refactor
  epic's philosophy. If a scene needs bespoke combat behaviour (e.g. Phaser's
  telegraph rules), use the smallest config seam.
- **Assumption:** "infinite lives" = the ship is never removed from the scene;
  each hit plays explosion VFX/SFX and re-spawns with a brief invulnerability
  window. Exact blink duration/invulnerability window is a tuning constant.
- **Assumption:** player auto-fire uses the default Cannon weapon (no power-ups
  in enemy gym scenes) — no weapon-drop UI added.
- **Risk:** single **scope creep** vector is power-up/weapon interaction,
  scoring, and lives HUD — explicitly out of scope; record as linked work items
  if requested.
- **Risk:** changes to the shared core scene affect all five scenes + the stub
  test suite — mitigate by keeping the config contract backward compatible and
  running the full suite before commit.
- **Risk:** Phaser collisions are manual (no engine) — false-positive edge cases
  in fast-motion bullet-vs-bullet checks; mitigate with radius-based checks per
  existing gym convention.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 (scope):** "Only the five existing scenes (E1–E5), leaving Boss for its
  own work item? Or should this item also plan for Boss's scene?"
  — **Answer (operator):** "existing" — cover only E1–E5; Boss
  (AH-0MT99QBDW001O7PE) stays a separate open item. Source: interactive reply,
  intake round 1.
- **Q2 (aim targeting):** "Should enemies now aim/fire/dive at the actual player
  position (live tracking), replacing the fixed bottom-centre stand-in?"
  — **Answer (operator):** "yes" — live tracking. Source: interactive reply,
  intake round 1.
- **Q3 (interaction):** "Should the player be keyboard-controllable, and should
  enemy bullets damage/destroy the player, or stay demonstration-only?"
  — **Answer (operator):** "player controlled. Bullets will hit the player (VFX
  and SFX), but the player will have infinite lives. Player bullets should
  destroy enemies and bullets". Source: interactive reply, intake round 1.
- **Q4 (firing input):** "Auto-fire in direction of travel (GDD §2.3, same as
  GymWeapons), or a manual fire button (e.g. Space)?"
  — **Answer (operator):** "auto" — auto-fire in direction of travel.
  Source: interactive reply, intake round 2.
- **Q5 (hit handling):** "On being hit — bullet + ship just play VFX/SFX with
  no gameplay state, or briefly explode/re-spawn (blink + invulnerability)?"
  — **Answer (operator):** "explode and respawn" — ship explodes and
  re-spawns with brief invulnerability. Source: interactive reply, intake
  round 2.
- **Q6 (demo buttons):** "With a live player, SHOOT becomes redundant — remove
  both EXPLODE and SHOOT buttons, or keep them?"
  — **Answer (operator):** "Leave them" — keep both; SHOOT keeps toggling
  enemy firing (L4+ simulation). Source: interactive reply, intake round 2.

Research summary: inspected `GymScout.ts`, `GymDiver.ts`, `GymTank.ts`,
`GymPhaser.ts`, `GymSwarm.ts` (all thin `GymFormationScene` subclasses, no
player), `core/GymFormationScene.ts` (shared spawn/HUD/update boilerplate,
config contract), enemy entities (`Scout/Diver/Swarm` hold fixed
`target = (width/2, height-40)`; `Tank` radial burst is direction-agnostic),
`GymWeapons.ts`/`GymPowerUps.ts`/`GymPlayer.ts` (established player wiring:
`new Player` → `setInput` → `physicsTick`, auto-fire via `tryFire` +
`createBulletsFromHeading`), `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` (core
library conventions, §5 seam-extension rules), worklog history
(`Create Enemy Gym Scene work items (AH-0MT987VA3005YBNK)` scope excluded
player ships; `Refactor Enemy Gym Scenes (AH-0MT985FOA008JWM9)` built the core
library).
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MTBOIIF6004GPY8** – Direction-neutral hexagon body shape (completed)
- **AH-0MTBD8H63003476N** – Implement linear deceleration in applyThrust movement model (completed)
- **AH-0MT7O8KCY0059RA5** – Game Design Document for AI_Hell (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `README.md` — matched: add, currently, enemy, fix, gym (+5 more)
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: add, enemy, fix, gym, lets (+4 more)
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: add, enemy, fix, gym, lets (+4 more)
